description:
Why this issue exists: server.rs resolve_user_id() maps a username to a DB user ID. When the username is not found in the database, it silently falls back to SINGLETON_USER_ID=1 with only a warn!() log. This means any authenticated user with a username that has not been provisioned in the DB will be silently granted access to user ID 1's data. In a multi-user deployment this is a cross-account data access bug.

What needs to be done: resolve_user_id() should return an Err (→ 403 or 404) when the user is not found, not silently substitute the singleton. The singleton fallback was appropriate when v1 was genuinely single-user-only, but now that the code has a real user lookup path the fallback is a latent authorization hole. Document the single-user-only scope constraint with a compile-time guard or an explicit config check.
title: resolve_user_id: silent fallback to SINGLETON_USER_ID=1 for unknown users
